title: Enabled member replaces an active turn grant over HTTP
description:
**Phase 1.** Parent epic `chatticus-598be4`. Child of the `chatticus-9a07e7` decision: Shape 1, per-task human grant.

## What to ship

An **enabled member** (Cognito user principal) can attach a closed `TaskCapabilityGrant` to an **active turn**. Clip to that member's ceiling. Worker `PUT /turns/{id}/grant` stays worker-only.

**One path: replace, not merge.** The body is a full closed grant (same as `Given a human task grants:`). It replaces `household_conversation_grant()` for that turn. Do not union tools with the conversation preset.

## Constraints

- Gherkin first (`turn_grant_widening.feature` or equivalent).
- New route on **`user_router`**, not `worker_router`.
- Deny when the grant exceeds member ceiling.
- Do not put `run_terminal` in the conversation preset.
- No web UI in this slice (`chatticus-753bd8`).

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Enabled member replaces an active turn grant
  As an enabled organization member
  I want to replace the active turn's closed grant
  So the bot may use tools I explicitly authorize for this task only

  Scenario: An enabled member replaces the conversation grant on an active turn
    Given tenant "anthus" user "ryan" has a bot named "Researcher"
    And user "ryan" of tenant "anthus" has started a turn with the household conversation grant
    When user "ryan" of tenant "anthus" replaces the active turn grant with:
      | field          | value                  |
      | tools          | read_workspace, browse |
      | origins        | https://docs.example.com |
      | recipients     |                        |
      | file_scopes    | /workspace             |
      | egress_classes | approved_origin_fetch  |
    Then the active turn grant is exactly that table

  Scenario: A grant that exceeds the member ceiling is refused
    Given tenant "anthus" user "ryan" is enabled with a limited ceiling
    When user "ryan" of tenant "anthus" replaces the active turn grant with tools beyond that ceiling
    Then the request is refused
    And the active turn still carries the household conversation grant

  Scenario: Worker PUT grant remains worker-only
    When an unauthenticated caller PUTs a turn grant on the user route
    Then the request is refused
```

## Done when

An authenticated org member can replace the turn grant over HTTP; an unauthenticated caller cannot; a grant that exceeds ceiling is refused; worker PUT remains worker-only.

comments.text:
Plan reviewed. Not authorized yet.

Blocking: do not treat a missing per-member `task_grant` standing row as unlimited. Reuse `MemberStanding` / role ceiling so `purchase` and `production_change` cannot be granted by a `member`. A grant-table factory into `MemberAuthorityCeiling` is fine; a second ceiling product is not.

HTTP grant replace is Gherkin only — delete `test_http_grant_persists_without_workspace_execute_route` rather than re-auth it in pytest. Move `capability_sink_wiring.feature` missing-turn grant to the user route. Retire unused `WorkerPlaneClient.put_grant` worker auth with the worker PUT.
